- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates or fails to capture volatility; increase forecast range or add upward bias.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is low; apply downward correction in first 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast increase to 5–7% max from prior day.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 85), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent low.
- If sentiment history shows no positive signals, model often fails to anticipate sudden drops; add 3–5% buffer below recent low for next 3–5 days.
- Forecast should not trend upward if sentiment is flat or negative for 5+ consecutive days; consider flat or slightly downward path.
